key_insight: Pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently model oxygen-defect scattering in AlN and explain how impurity complexes suppress thermal conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to predict and tune thermal transport in AlN for thermal management applications while reducing reliance on costly first-principles simulations.
method: Benchmark pretrained MLIPs against DFT for phonon dispersions and pristine thermal conductivity
Use a fine-tuned SevenNet-Nano model in molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo annealing to form defect complexes
Extract defect scattering from SED linewidths and feed it into iterative BTE thermal-conductivity calculations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that SED-derived defect scattering rates agree reasonably with harmonic T-matrix predictions at low oxygen content and that the resulting thermal conductivities match experimental trends.
watch_item: The approach becomes less reliable at high oxygen concentrations where scattering no longer scales linearly, indicating limits of independent-defect and pristine-phonon assumptions.
paper_title: Defect-limited thermal transport in AlN using pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials
